```{r}
# This file uses the cleaned modeling dataset created in the leaderboard file.
# The leaderboard file already calculated the runner and catcher metrics, so this file focuses only on modeling Safe% and building the model-based scoreboard graphic.

# The goal is to compare a few possible models, choose a final Safe% model, and use that model to find plays that beat expectation.
# Those plays become scoreboard prompts such as GOOD SLIDE! or GOOD TAG!

library(tidyverse)
library(pROC)
library(randomForest)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(ggplot2)
model_data <- readRDS("steal_modeling_data.rds")
```


## Train/test split

```{r}
# Split the plays into training and testing data.
# The model learns from the training set.
# The test set is saved for final evaluation.

set.seed(123)

train_index <- sample(
  1:nrow(model_data),
  size = floor(0.70 * nrow(model_data))
)

train_data <- model_data[train_index, ]
test_data  <- model_data[-train_index, ]

# Check that both Safe and Out plays appear in both sets.
# AUC cannot be calculated if either set only has one outcome type.

train_data %>%
  count(outcome_model)

test_data %>%
  count(outcome_model)
```

## Thresholds and evaluation functions

```{r}
# The models return a Safe%, not a direct Safe/Out decision.
# To turn that probability into a prediction, we need a cutoff.

# Example:
# If the threshold is 0.60, then:
#   Safe% >= 60% predicts Safe
#   Safe% < 60% predicts Out

# Instead of assuming 50%, this function tests thresholds from 5% to 95% and picks the one with the best balanced accuracy on the training data.
# Balanced accuracy is useful because it rewards the model for identifying both Safe and Out plays instead of only favoring the more common outcome.

choose_best_threshold <- function(actual, prob) {
  
  map_dfr(seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.01), function(threshold) {
    
    pred <- if_else(prob >= threshold, 1, 0)
    
    tp <- sum(pred == 1 & actual == 1)
    tn <- sum(pred == 0 & actual == 0)
    fp <- sum(pred == 1 & actual == 0)
    fn <- sum(pred == 0 & actual == 1)
    
    sensitivity <- if_else(tp + fn == 0, NA_real_, tp / (tp + fn))
    specificity <- if_else(tn + fp == 0, NA_real_, tn / (tn + fp))
    accuracy <- (tp + tn) / length(actual)
    balanced_accuracy <- mean(c(sensitivity, specificity), na.rm = TRUE)
    
    tibble(
      threshold = threshold,
      accuracy = accuracy,
      sensitivity = sensitivity,
      specificity = specificity,
      balanced_accuracy = balanced_accuracy
    )
  }) %>%
    arrange(desc(balanced_accuracy), desc(accuracy)) %>%
    slice(1)
}

# This function evaluates each model on the held-out test set.
# It uses the threshold selected from the training set, then calculates:
#   accuracy = overall percent correct
#   sensitivity = how well the model identifies Safe plays
#   specificity = how well the model identifies Out plays
#   balanced accuracy = average of sensitivity and specificity
#   AUC = how well the model ranks Safe plays above Out plays by probability

evaluate_model <- function(actual, prob, threshold, model_name) {
  
  pred <- if_else(prob >= threshold, 1, 0)
  
  tp <- sum(pred == 1 & actual == 1)
  tn <- sum(pred == 0 & actual == 0)
  fp <- sum(pred == 1 & actual == 0)
  fn <- sum(pred == 0 & actual == 1)
  
  accuracy <- (tp + tn) / length(actual)
  sensitivity <- if_else(tp + fn == 0, NA_real_, tp / (tp + fn))
  specificity <- if_else(tn + fp == 0, NA_real_, tn / (tn + fp))
  balanced_accuracy <- mean(c(sensitivity, specificity), na.rm = TRUE)
  
# Build the ROC curve using the actual result and predicted Safe%.
roc_curve <- pROC::roc(
  response = actual,
  predictor = prob,
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Calculate the area under the ROC curve.
auc_value <- pROC::auc(roc_curve)

# Convert the AUC object into a normal number for the results table.
auc_value <- as.numeric(auc_value)
  
  tibble(
    model = model_name,
    threshold = threshold,
    test_accuracy = accuracy,
    test_sensitivity = sensitivity,
    test_specificity = specificity,
    test_balanced_accuracy = balanced_accuracy,
    test_auc = auc_value
  )
}
```

## Model 1: Logistic Regression

```{r}
# Logistic regression is the baseline model.
# It is simple and easy to explain, but it assumes a more linear relationship.

logit_model <- glm(
  safe_binary ~ top_speed_mph + jump + pop_time + throw_velo,
  data = train_data,
  family = binomial
)

# Predicted Safe% for the training and test sets.

train_logit_prob <- predict(
  logit_model,
  newdata = train_data,
  type = "response"
)

test_logit_prob <- predict(
  logit_model,
  newdata = test_data,
  type = "response"
)

# Pick the best threshold using training-set probabilities only.

logit_threshold <- choose_best_threshold(
  actual = train_data$safe_binary,
  prob = train_logit_prob
)

# Evaluate logistic regression on the held-out test set.

logit_eval <- evaluate_model(
  actual = test_data$safe_binary,
  prob = test_logit_prob,
  threshold = logit_threshold$threshold[1],
  model_name = "Logistic Regression"
)

logit_threshold
logit_eval
```

## Model 2: Decision tree

```{r}
# The decision tree is a simple nonlinear comparison model.
# Unlike logistic regression, it can split plays into rule-based groups.
# For example, it can separate plays with fast runners or slow pop times.
# This gives a useful comparison before trying a random forest.

set.seed(123)

tree_model <- rpart(
  outcome_factor ~ top_speed_mph + jump + pop_time + throw_velo,
  data = train_data,
  method = "class",
  control = rpart.control(
    cp = 0.01,
    minsplit = 10
  )
)

# Plot the tree so the model logic can be interpreted visually.

rpart.plot(tree_model)

# Predicted Safe% from the tree model.

train_tree_prob <- predict(
  tree_model,
  newdata = train_data,
  type = "prob"
)[, "Safe"]

test_tree_prob <- predict(
  tree_model,
  newdata = test_data,
  type = "prob"
)[, "Safe"]

# Pick the best threshold using the training set.

tree_threshold <- choose_best_threshold(
  actual = train_data$safe_binary,
  prob = train_tree_prob
)

# Evaluate the decision tree on the held-out test set.

tree_eval <- evaluate_model(
  actual = test_data$safe_binary,
  prob = test_tree_prob,
  threshold = tree_threshold$threshold[1],
  model_name = "Decision Tree"
)

tree_threshold
tree_eval
```

## Model 3: Random forest model

```{r}
# Random forest is tested as a more flexible comparison model.
# It builds many decision trees and averages them together.
# This can help capture nonlinear relationships between runner and catcher metrics, but it can also overfit when the dataset is small or noisy.

set.seed(123)

rf_model <- randomForest(
  outcome_factor ~ top_speed_mph + jump + pop_time + throw_velo,
  data = train_data,
  ntree = 500,
  mtry = 2,
  nodesize = 5,
  importance = TRUE
)

rf_model

## Random forest threshold

# The random forest also gives a Safe% for each play.
# For threshold selection, I use the out-of-bag probabilities from the random forest.
# These are better than regular training predictions because each row is predicted by trees that did not train on that row.

train_rf_prob <- rf_model$votes[, "Safe"]

test_rf_prob <- predict(
  rf_model,
  newdata = test_data,
  type = "prob"
)[, "Safe"]

rf_threshold <- choose_best_threshold(
  actual = train_data$safe_binary,
  prob = train_rf_prob
)

rf_eval <- evaluate_model(
  actual = test_data$safe_binary,
  prob = test_rf_prob,
  threshold = rf_threshold$threshold[1],
  model_name = "Random Forest"
)

rf_threshold
rf_eval
```

```{r}
## Compare model results

# This table compares the three model types on the same test set.
# Test AUC measures how well the model ranks actual Safe plays above actual Out plays.
# Balanced accuracy checks whether the chosen threshold separates both classes well.
# The final model is chosen based on both performance and whether the probabilities make sense for a scoreboard graphic.

model_comparison <- bind_rows(
  logit_eval,
  tree_eval,
  rf_eval
) %>%
  arrange(desc(test_auc), desc(test_balanced_accuracy))

model_comparison
```

## Final Safe% Model:

```{r}
# Based on the model comparison, logistic regression is used as the final Safe% model.
# It gives smoother probability estimates than the decision tree and is easier to explain in a fan-facing scoreboard setting
# The model is not meant to replace the call on the field. It is used to find expectation-breaking plays that can be highlighted for fans.

final_threshold <- logit_threshold$threshold[1]

# Refit the final logistic model using all available labeled plays.
# This gives the final Safe% model the most data possible before generating scoreboard examples.

final_logit_model <- glm(
  safe_binary ~ top_speed_mph + jump + pop_time + throw_velo,
  data = model_data,
  family = binomial
)

safe_probability_table <- model_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Predicted probability that the runner is safe.
    safe_prob = predict(
      final_logit_model,
      newdata = model_data,
      type = "response"
    ),
    # Convert probability to a scoreboard-friendly percentage.
    safe_pct = round(100 * safe_prob, 0),
    # Convert Safe% into a Safe/Out prediction using the selected threshold.
    model_prediction = if_else(
      safe_prob >= final_threshold,
      "Safe",
      "Out"
    )
  )

safe_probability_table %>%
  select(
    game_string,
    play_per_game,
    runner,
    catcher,
    outcome_model,
    safe_pct,
    model_prediction,
    top_speed_mph,
    jump,
    pop_time,
    throw_velo
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(safe_pct)) %>%
  head(10)

saveRDS(safe_probability_table, "safe_probability_table.rds")
```
```{r}
## Model spotlight plays

# These are plays where the model expectation and the actual result disagree.
# They are the most useful plays for scoreboard storytelling.

# GOOD TAG:
# The model expected the runner to be safe, but the actual result was Out.

# GOOD SLIDE:
# The model expected the runner to be out, but the actual result was Safe.

# These labels are fan-facing prompts, not definitive claims about slide or tag quality.

model_moments <- safe_probability_table %>%
  mutate(
    scoreboard_label = case_when(
      safe_prob >= 0.70 & outcome_model == "Out" ~ "GOOD TAG!",
      safe_prob <= 0.40 & outcome_model == "Safe" ~ "GOOD SLIDE!",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    
    model_story = case_when(
      scoreboard_label == "GOOD TAG!" ~
        "Model expected the runner to be safe, but the defense created an out.",
      
      scoreboard_label == "GOOD SLIDE!" ~
        "Model expected the runner to be out, but the runner beat the expectation.",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(scoreboard_label))

model_moments %>%
  select(
    game_string,
    play_per_game,
    runner,
    catcher,
    outcome_model,
    safe_pct,
    model_prediction,
    scoreboard_label,
    model_story,
    top_speed_mph,
    jump,
    pop_time,
    throw_velo
  ) %>%
  arrange(scoreboard_label, desc(safe_pct))

model_moments %>%
  count(scoreboard_label)

saveRDS(model_moments, "model_moments.rds")
```

```{r}
# Pick one example GOOD SLIDE! play for the scoreboard graphic.
# This selects the Safe play with the lowest model Safe%, meaning it beat the model expectation the most.

good_slide_example <- model_moments %>%
  filter(scoreboard_label == "GOOD SLIDE!") %>%
  arrange(safe_prob) %>%
  slice(1)

good_slide_example
```

```{r}
make_model_scoreboard <- function(play_row, output_file = NULL) {
  # Create the text labels that will appear on the scoreboard.
  plot_data <- play_row %>%
    mutate(
      safe_pct_label = paste0(safe_pct, "%"),
      actual_label = paste("Actual Result:", outcome_model),
      model_label = paste("Model Prediction:", model_prediction),
      runner_label = paste("Runner:", runner),
      catcher_label = paste("Catcher:", catcher),
      speed_label = paste("Top Speed:", round(top_speed_mph, 1), "mph"),
      jump_label = paste("Jump:", round(jump, 1), "ft/s gained"),
      pop_label = paste("Pop Time:", round(pop_time, 2), "sec"),
      throw_label = paste("Throw Velo:", round(throw_velo, 1), "mph")
    )
   # Build a one-play scoreboard graphic.
  # This is separate from the top-10 leaderboards because it highlights a model-based story rather than a leaderboard ranking. 
  p <- ggplot(plot_data) +
    # Background and header.
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#07111F") +
    
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 100, ymin = 85, ymax = 100,
             fill = "#12355B") +
    # Main scoreboard title.
    annotate("text", x = 50, y = 95, label = plot_data$scoreboard_label[1],
             color = "white", size = 14, fontface = "bold") +
    
    annotate("text", x = 50, y = 88.5, 
             label = "This play beat expectation!",
             color = "#D8E2F3", size = 5) +
# Safe% panel. 
    annotate("rect", xmin = 8, xmax = 92, ymin = 60, ymax = 80,
             fill = "#D99A25", color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    
    annotate("text", x = 50, y = 74, label = "SAFE%", color = "white",
             size = 7, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 50, y = 66, label = plot_data$safe_pct_label[1],
             color = "white", size = 16, fontface = "bold") +
# Actual result and model prediction panels.  
    annotate("rect", xmin = 8, xmax = 45, ymin = 38, ymax = 56,
             fill = "#0B1B2B", color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 55, xmax = 92, ymin = 38, ymax = 56,
             fill = "#0B1B2B", color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    
    annotate("text", x = 26.5, y = 51, label = plot_data$actual_label[1],
             color = "white", size = 5.5, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 73.5, y = 51, label = plot_data$model_label[1],
             color = "white", size = 5.5, fontface = "bold") +
    
    annotate("text", x = 26.5, y = 44, label = plot_data$runner_label[1],
             color = "#D8E2F3", size = 5) +
    annotate("text", x = 73.5, y = 44, label = plot_data$catcher_label[1],
             color = "#D8E2F3", size = 5) +
# Tracking metric panel. 
    annotate("rect", xmin = 8, xmax = 92, ymin = 10, ymax = 32,
             fill = "#0B1B2B", color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    
    annotate("text", x = 20, y = 27, label = plot_data$speed_label[1],
             color = "white", size = 5, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 20, y = 18, label = plot_data$jump_label[1],
             color = "#D8E2F3", size = 4.8) +
    
    annotate("text", x = 68, y = 27, label = plot_data$pop_label[1],
             color = "white", size = 5, fontface = "bold") +
    annotate("text", x = 68, y = 18, label = plot_data$throw_label[1],
             color = "#D8E2F3", size = 4.8) +
# Footer.    
    annotate("text", x = 50, y = 4,
             label = "STOLEN BASE SPOTLIGHT | MODEL EXPECTATION BOARD",
             color = "#AFC4E8", size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
    
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 100), ylim = c(0, 100), expand = FALSE) +
    theme_void()
# Save the graphic if an output filename is provided.  
  if (!is.null(output_file)) {
    ggsave(output_file, p, width = 16, height = 9, dpi = 150)
  }
  
  p
}
```

```{r}
# Create and save the final example scoreboard graphic.

make_model_scoreboard(
  play_row = good_slide_example,
  output_file = "good_slide_scoreboard.png"
)
```
